subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a militarized cyberpunk armored truck with a turret and neon accents, deciding it can stay a mostly static model without complex joints since it's a vehicle prop.

I'm working out the full dimensions and layout—an 8-wheeled, four-axle truck roughly 8m long, 2.8m wide, with specific wheel radius, axle spacing, and body width so everything aligns correctly in a y-up, z-forward coordinate system. I'm also setting up helper functions for boxes and parts, deciding on paint and texture approaches like gunmetal hull paneling, hazard stripe decals, and HUD screen textures using the glow and clockwork kits.

Now I'm sketching the chassis as a long flat box, then shaping the cab by extruding a sloped windscreen profile defined as a series of (z,y) coordinate points to get the angled front and roof lines right.

Normalizing that slope direction to get the windscreen plane's facing axis, sizing it at 2.2 by 1.17 with a slight outward offset, and giving it a cyan scanline visor texture with a subtle glow for a HUD-like look.

Adding dark glass side windows at the cab's half-width, then building the front with a heavy ram bumper box featuring hazard-stripe texture, an angled plate wedge, and a glowing cyan-white headlight strip along the sloped front fascia.

Still shaping the vehicle body...

I'm adding side skirts and armor plates with glowing neon underglow strips, plus cyberpunk emblem decals on the side panels with text like "MIL-TEK 2077" and hazard stripe details.

For the turret, I'm building a ring base with twin barrel cylinders oriented along the z-axis, a sensor dome, and a glowing red eye lens, then adding angled missile pod racks on the rear roof with tube-shaped missile ends.

Writing pod geometry helper...

Now I'm designing the wheel assemblies: dark tire cylinders, steel rims, and a thin glowing hub ring, trying to keep part counts manageable across all eight wheels.

Building the tread blocks...

Now I'm thinking through the suspension components — axle cylinders at the wheel height, shock absorber cylinders linking axle to chassis, and fender shapes above the wheels.

Working out wheel placement so they sit at the body's outer edge without clashing with the bed hull, adjusting half-width dimensions so the wheels sink slightly into the body for a natural look, then adding fender boxes above each wheel to cover them.

For the cab roof I'm planning a sensor mast, antenna array, a lathe-built satellite dish, and a light bar rack, while behind the cab I'm placing twin vertical exhaust stacks with glowing orange heat rings at their tips.

Resolving collisions, I'm moving the exhaust cylinders outward to avoid overlapping the bed and cab geometry, then adding reactive armor tile grids on the cab sides and bed fronts plus inset door panels, merging each set into single parts per side. For bed greebles I'm planning vents with glowing grille textures and cable conduits along the sides.

Now I'm sketching the rear assembly—a ramp door with warning lights, red glow strips, bumper, and caution-stencil decals facing backward—along with under-chassis details like a driveshaft and side fuel tanks positioned between the second and third axles, checking their dimensions fit without clipping the wheels or bed floor.

Now I'm placing sensor camera pods and antennas on the cab and bumper corners, then working out the turret: a cylindrical base ring, a rotating body box mounted on the bed, and twin barrels positioned on top.

I'm also adding barrel shrouds, muzzle brakes, side ammo drums, and a domed sensor head with a glowing red eye and targeting laser. For cyberpunk flavor I'm thinking through neon strip accents—cyan edges, magenta underglow, orange warning lights, a holographic plate—and settling on a gunmetal paint scheme with lighter top panels and grime-darkened undersides.

For the hull I'm layering digital camo patches in dark teal and black tones, then running that through a paneling effect with rivets for texture, paired with iron-toned armor accents and magenta/cyan/amber stripe colors. Now I'm listing out the texture assets I need: hazard stripes, a winged emblem, vent grilles, rims, a windshield HUD with scanlines, side glass, a rear plate, and a neon sign.

I'm deciding on neon strip text like "KOMOREBI-ARMS" and "VANGUARD 2077" for the bed side, plus a radar display and hex-grid panel textures. For glowing neon signs I'm keeping the background dark and opaque while the text itself glows, being careful that glow effects on painted materials can throw errors but work fine on textured or flat-color parts. I'm working out the texture mapping for side panels, figuring out which axis and direction orients the plane so the texture reads correctly from the viewer's position outside the vehicle.

Confirms viewer's right is +X, matching the model's left side — orientation checks out for the rear plane too. Now I'm writing helper functions to compute each plane's orientation.

Still writing helpers...

Now I'm placing the axle positions along z for the four wheels, with the front two steerable, and checking wheel x-offset against cab width and fender clearance so everything fits.

I'm sizing the chassis frame box and adjusting its y-position and z-length to match the wheelbase, then checking that the cab hull bottom aligns with the chassis top so there's no visible gap between them.

Now I'm adding the front bumper as a plain box with a hazard-striped decal plane placed just in front of it, then starting the snowplow wedge geometry by extruding a side profile defined by a few y-z coordinate points.

Placing the headlights and grille on the front fascia, with glow boxes for the lights and a dark vented grille panel positioned slightly forward of the cab face.

Now I'm adding a neon edge-glow helper for cyan accent rods along the cab and body, plus underglow strips running along the sides of the body between the wheels.

I should reposition the tanks slightly outward so they clear the chassis box, then only place the underglow strip along the larger gap plus a magenta pair near the front, skipping the smaller conflicting gaps. Now I'm turning to the bed side plating geometry.

For the side armor, I'm planning three protruding slabs with small gaps showing neon vertical rods between them, spaced along the bed's length, each panel roughly 1.3 wide and 1.1 tall. I'm thinking of adding a decal or neon sign reading "VANGUARD 2077" on the rear panel, with the other panels reserved for additional detailing.

I'm also adding a stretched hazard-stripe texture plane along the bed's lower edge, and planning roof details like vent boxes, a hatch, cargo rack rails, missile pods near the rear, a turret, and an antenna.

For the cab roof I'm placing a lightbar with alternating amber/blue segments, a satellite dish, twin mast antennas with glowing tips, a rooftop sensor ball with a lens, and side mirrors with small glowing screens.

Now I'm adding door seam details using thin dark rods and protruding panel boxes to suggest paneling and window outlines.

For the rear, I'm placing red glow strips as taillights, a textured warning plate near the tailgate reading "KX-2077 / ARMED", and a rear bumper box with a hazard-striped plane to finish off the back end.

Underneath, I'm modeling the drivetrain: a driveshaft cylinder running lengthwise, differential boxes and spheres at each axle, axle cylinders, and shock absorbers with coiled springs swept along a path between the body and wheel mounts.

Since this is a static vehicle rather than a rigged creature, I can skip joints entirely and just sweep the coil geometry directly for the shocks, keeping coil turns and side counts low for efficiency. No need to rig the wheels for spinning either since that's not required for vehicle models.

Now I'm sketching the turret: a ring-shaped base cylinder, then a chunky angled hull body on top.

Still writing extrude profile...

I'm thinking about adding a small docked quadcopter drone on the roof rear with rotor discs glowing cyan, plus exhaust stacks, a rear antenna whip, and simple tow hooks instead of a winch at the front bumper.

Now I'm placing round spotlights and fog lights at the bumper corners, a magenta underglow strip along the front bottom, and double-checking the tire geometry so the wheels touch the ground convincingly despite the cylinder's polygon approximation.

Checking worst-case rotation between blocks confirms the lowest point stays safely near or just above the floor, so that's acceptable. For the rim and tire, I'm using a core cylinder with a wider tire sidewall of the same color, placing the rim face slightly outside the tire width and applying the rim texture within a smaller circular radius, with the inner side hidden from view.

I'll add a small hub cap cylinder that protrudes slightly on each side in steel, though it's optional. For the rim texture I'm sketching an SVG with a dark circle, grey spokes, and a cyan inner ring glow, keeping it just colored rather than actually glowing. I'm settling on a limited color palette—gunmetal tones, steel greys, black, a teal, and accent colors like cyan, magenta, amber, red, white, and yellow—to keep the total flat count under 64.

Now I'm defining more materials: a hull with camo-style patches, a plated metal look, and a grimy dark deck paint that mixes gunmetal with lightening on upward faces and added grime and noise near the bottom edges.

I'm laying out small tiled panels along the side with gaps, merging them into a single olive-toned part, and placing it at the origin without a bone since there are no joints in this static model.

Now I'm writing a helper function to merge boxes, importing the builder utilities and clockwork kit pieces I need, then drafting the hazard-stripe SVG texture.

For the vent I'll add grey slats without glow, keeping the glow effect reserved for the emblem ring and neon sign lines instead. The emblem will have a cyan ring, hex shape, and bold monospace "V-77" text on a transparent background, then I'll move on to designing the neon sign with a dark rectangle base.

Now I'm sketching the neon sign border and text in magenta and cyan, then shifting to the HUD windshield -- an opaque glass gradient with subtle diagonal reflections and thin cyan HUD lines sized to stay visible at the final raster resolution, including a reticle circle and some text elements.

Still building out the rim wheel texture with its spokes, hub, and lug dots, plus the rear plate with hazard stripe and warning text.

Now I'm sketching the mirror screens as flat glowing color planes rather than textured, then starting the actual build function with a builder instance and helper functions for creating boxes and other geometry.

Yes, flat textures work fine with b.part. I'm setting up mirror loops for left/right symmetry and defining wheel axle positions, then generating tread block geometry by rotating boxes around the axle and merging them into a single tire mesh, slightly oversized to protrude from the tire surface.

Still working through the radial sizing to avoid z-fighting between tread blocks, tire core, and rim pieces, settling on specific radii so the hubcap protrudes correctly without clipping into the tread.

Now I'm planning the fender geometry — boxes positioned over the wheel tops with angled lip extensions and outer skirt plates so the wheels remain visible beneath, plus adding rear mud flap boxes behind each wheel.

Working through the suspension system: axle cylinders, differential spheres, leaf spring boxes positioned near the chassis edges, vertical shock cylinders, and a swept coil spring geometry connecting the axle to the chassis.

I'm adding steering link rods for the front axles, defining the main chassis box, a long driveshaft cylinder running through the frame, and starting an extruded cab shape with hull paint.

Now I'm working out the bed and bumper extrusions with plate-colored paint, then placing the cab-over details -- calculating the windscreen's slanted plane position, width, and offset so it sits flush against the sloped front.

I'm also sketching out smaller cab pieces: wiper rods, an armored visor brow above the windscreen, side window panels, and considering whether blast shutters are worth adding at the window edges.

Now I'm working out the side window dimensions more precisely and placing door seam rods and ERA tile arrays along the lower cab sides for armor detail.

I'm checking that the fenders over the wheels don't badly overlap the tile arrays, then shaping the cab's front fascia with its slight forward bulge between the chin and bridge, positioning the headlight accordingly.

Now I'm placing the headlight strips, central grille box, and vent plane on the front fascia, plus a thin DRL rod running across near the bridge height, and starting the windscreen wiper rods.

For the cab roof, I'm adding a light bar made of a base box plus glow segments in red and blue, then working out a satellite dish using a lathe shape with a tilted axis, figuring out the radius/height outline points to form a shallow bowl.

Still writing turret and sensor details...

Now I'm adding roof slope details and bed vents as small boxes near the rear.

Checking rotor clearance against the drone's arm span, then adding a small hatch cylinder on top and bed side panels with vertical neon rod accents positioned in the gaps between panels.

Still arranging decal placements...

Now I'm working out the rear bumper, hazard plane, and glowing tail light boxes positioned at the back face of the vehicle.

Adding exhaust pipes with heat-shield bands, glowing orange rings, and mounting brackets...

Skipping the side skirts, I'm moving to the turret design: positioning its center, defining a convex extruded profile for the body shape, and setting up barrel shrouds with detail boxes.

Now I'm working out the turret's base ring, gun mantlet box, and barrel cylinder placement, carefully adjusting the z-coordinates so the barrels clear the cab roof and align properly with the mantlet front.

Adding barrel shrouds, muzzle brakes, glowing cyan tip discs, and glowing coil rings along the barrels, then starting on the ammo drum geometry...

Now I'm placing the sensor dome on the turret top with a forward-offset glowing red lens, adding thin antenna rods with glow tips, and setting up a helper function for positioning weapon pods using directional vectors.

Still placing missile pods and nose cones...

Now I'm sketching the drone geometry: a small body box, rod arms extending to four corners, and glowing cyan rotor cylinders at each corner.

I'm adding glowing eye spheres, landing legs, and cyan accent rods along the cab roof edges, then sketching bumper details like spotlights, tow hooks, and a bull bar cage made of crossing rods.

Skipping cab underbody details since tires are sorted. I'm thinking about adding a stencil decal on the cab door, like an "A-07" marking with bold text and small chevrons, placing it on the lower door panel and reserving front/rear sections for ERA tile patterns so they don't overlap.

I'm sketching a small door decal SVG with yellow "TK-07" text on a transparent background, then moving on to bumper hazard details and a rear antenna mast with glowing amber/cyan tips above the cab roof. I'm also tallying up total part counts across wheels, axles, and other components to keep the build organized.

Now I'm double-checking the API conventions for part placement, rotation, and color options before writing the actual build code, confirming details like extrude coloring, lathe geometry parameters, and how glow effects attach to parts and rods.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing SVG code...

Writing paint and panel logic...
